clue.text: Somebody outside church with local deputy

indicators.note: outside means the important-person letters go around the church abbreviation

parts.note: a somebody is a VIP, a very important person
CE is the Church of England
a local is a resident of the area

explanation.surface: A notable figure stands outside a church alongside a neighbour, who happens to be an assistant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local' reads as an adjective but is a noun here: a person who lives nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: A vice-president is a second-in-command who stands in for the president, a classic deputy role.

clue.text: Do they show parts near the bone?

definitions.text: Do they show parts near the bone?

parts.words: Do they show parts near the bone?
parts.note: fractions such as 3/4 show parts of a whole, and humour that is near the bone is crude or vulgar

explanation.surface: A butcher's question about cuts of meat close to the bone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Near the bone' means risqué, so a vulgar thing showing parts is a common fraction written as numerator over denominator.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordinary fractions such as two-thirds display parts of a whole, and 'near the bone' is an idiom for coarse or crude.

clue.text: Navigator's enthralling hunt for swells

indicators.note: enthralling means holding captive, so the navigator's word holds the search word inside it

parts.note: a cox steers a rowing boat, so the navigator's is COX'S
to comb an area is to hunt through it thoroughly

explanation.surface: A navigator becomes absorbed in a search for large ocean waves.
explanation.definitionFit: Swells here are dandies, conceited showy men, and coxcombs is an old word for such fops.

clue.text: Hard to finish puzzle without Queen Victoria

indicators.note: to finish puts the hardness letter at the end of the remaining letters
without means the royal letters are dropped from the word for a puzzle

parts.note: a poser is a puzzling question
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword queen
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Without the old queen, this puzzle is hard to complete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen Victoria' reads as one person, but 'Queen' is ER and 'Victoria' is the definition: Victoria Beckham was Posh Spice of the Spice Girls.
explanation.definitionFit: Victoria Beckham's nickname in the Spice Girls pop group was Posh Spice, so the singer is known as Posh.

clue.text: Extremely fine cuts in my cafe, oddly what the butcher lacks?

indicators.note: cuts means the outer letters of fine slice into the jumbled letters
oddly signals that the letters of 'in my cafe' come out in a strange order
extremely points to the extreme, outermost letters of fine

explanation.surface: A butcher's shop serves very fine cuts of meat in a café, oddly enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butcher' reads as a meat trader, but it is 'more butch'. 'Oddly' rearranges IN MY CAFE into EFMINACY, and FE, the ends of 'fine', go inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone butcher, that is more butch and macho, would lack girlish softness or unmanliness.

clue.text: Sound is a little faint, actually

indicators.note: a little says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A noise is barely audible, really just a slight whisper.
explanation.definitionFit: Sound in the sense of undamaged or whole, as in safe and sound.

clue.text: Talk on camera, mix freely!

indicators.note: freely says the letters of the preceding words are mixed without restraint into a new order

explanation.surface: A director urges people on screen to chat and mingle without inhibition.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of TALK ON CAMERA MIX are rearranged, and the clue itself ends in the very punctuation it describes.
explanation.definitionFit: The '!' punctuation that closes the clue is this symbol, used after an exclamation.

clue.text: About to enter not just any posh location

indicators.note: to enter means the short word for about goes inside the article

parts.note: the definite article, as opposed to 'a', means a particular thing, not just any
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Being on the subject of breaking into some exclusive upmarket spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Posh location' means the place in this grid where POSH is entered: it is 3-down.
explanation.definitionFit: A cross-reference: the word posh is the answer to the clue numbered 3 in this grid.

clue.text: Mountain road parts as long as river

indicators.note: parts means the road abbreviation splits the conjunction open

parts.note: while means as long as, during the time that
St, street, is a road
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A mountain road divides wherever it runs alongside a river.
explanation.walkthrough: Whistler is a ski mountain in British Columbia, Canada.
explanation.definitionFit: Whistler Mountain is a peak in the Coast Mountains of British Columbia, home to a famous ski resort.

clue.text: Around start of lesson I spell 'curlicue'

indicators.note: around means the word for a spell goes round the following letters

parts.note: a hex is a magic spell or curse

indicators.note: start of takes the opening letter of lesson

explanation.surface: A teacher spells out the word curlicue near the beginning of a lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spell' looks like spelling a word aloud, but it is a witch's curse, HEX.
explanation.definitionFit: A curlicue is a decorative curl or twist, and a spiral coil is that shape.

clue.text: It's used after mostly scary spins

definitions.text: It's used after mostly scary spins

indicators.note: spins means the letters are whirled round into a new order
mostly means all but the last letter of after is used

explanation.surface: Motor racing: a vehicle sent out after cars spin off alarmingly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' drops the last letter of 'after', and 'spins' rearranges the result with 'scary'; the whole clue also describes the vehicle's job.
explanation.definitionFit: In motor racing a pace vehicle is sent onto the track to slow the field after crashes or spins.

clue.text: Plant pots fooled dog

indicators.note: pots means puts into a pot, so the planting word holds the other inside it

parts.note: to sow is to plant seeds
had means fooled or tricked, as in 'you've been had'

explanation.surface: Someone potting plants is tricked by a dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant pots' reads as flowerpots; 'pots' is a verb meaning encloses.
explanation.definitionFit: To dog someone is to follow them closely, the same as tailing them like a detective.

clue.text: Apparently I returned and consumed waste

parts.note: 'I returned' means 'I came back', and read literally that is I CAME written backwards
ate means consumed

explanation.surface: Coming home, a person finds they ate and wasted away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Apparently' flags a literal reading: 'I returned' is 'I came back', so I CAME is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To waste away is to grow thin, and the verb here means to become abnormally thin.

clue.text: Soft light so weird on something in fire?

parts.note: p, piano, means soft in music

indicators.note: weird signals that the letters of 'light so' are jumbled oddly

explanation.surface: A soft light glowing strangely on something burning in a fire.
explanation.walkthrough: Phlogiston was the 17th-18th century theory's substance thought to be released in burning.
explanation.definitionFit: Old chemistry held that a substance contained in every combustible material escaped as it burned.

clue.text: Abandoned port in difficulty, what?

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship

indicators.note: in means the query word sits inside the word for difficulty

parts.note: a bind is a difficulty or awkward situation
eh? means what?

explanation.surface: Someone asks, puzzled, about a harbour deserted in a crisis.
explanation.definitionFit: To be abandoned is to be deserted or not taken along when others go.

clue.text: Girl, 14

parts.note: the answer to 14 is 'left behind', whose first word gives L, the abbreviation for left
the second word of 14, behind, means the backside or bottom, an ass

explanation.walkthrough: 14-across, LEFT BEHIND, is read as instructions: L (left) then ASS (behind, the backside).
explanation.definitionFit: A lass is a young woman, chiefly in Scottish and Northern English use.

clue.text: Nun's kept in the dark?

indicators.note: kept means the little word is held inside the word for a nun

parts.note: a nun is a sister; the 's is 'has', the nun having kept something

explanation.surface: A nun has been kept uninformed about something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kept in the dark' reads as one idiom, but 'kept' is the container signal and 'dark' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinister means dark in the sense of evil, threatening or ominous.

clue.text: Naked girl reportedly in capital city

indicators.note: reportedly means what follows is how the words sound when spoken

parts.note: naked is nude and the girl is Ellie, so nude Ellie

explanation.surface: A tabloid story about a naked young woman in the capital.
explanation.definitionFit: New Delhi is the capital city of India.

clue.text: Butter spread by old tramp

indicators.note: spread by means the word for a butter is pushed apart by the abbreviation

parts.note: a butter is something that butts, such as a ram

explanation.surface: Butter is spread on bread by a vagrant from long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butter' looks like the dairy spread, but it is one who butts: a ram.
explanation.definitionFit: To tramp is to walk or wander about, which is to rove or wander aimlessly.

clue.text: Nodule I fitted in plastic connector

indicators.note: fitted in means the single letter is placed inside the rearranged letters
plastic means mouldable, so the letters of connector are reshaped

explanation.surface: A small lump fitted inside a plastic connector.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plastic' rearranges CONNECTOR, and I is placed inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A concretion is a hard lump of mineral matter formed in rock or the body, a nodule.

clue.text: Deer — it's one with foot raised

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the letters are read upwards, that is backwards

parts.note: the it of 'it's' is taken as written; the 's is a link meaning is
one is I, the Roman numeral
a paw is an animal's foot

explanation.surface: A deer stands with one hoof lifted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raised' turns IT I PAW upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The wapiti is the large North American elk, a member of the deer family.

clue.text: A Duran Duran album opened by ugly old reprobate

indicators.note: opened by means the old word comes first, at the opening

parts.note: loth is an archaic form meaning loathsome or hateful
Rio is a 1982 album by the British pop band Duran Duran

explanation.surface: A Duran Duran record starts with an ugly old rogue.
explanation.definitionFit: A Lothario is a seducer and rake, a man of loose morals.

clue.text: Substitute's lofted pass? I'm not sure

definitions.note: the definition is 'Substitute' with 's meaning is

indicators.note: lofted means raised up, so in this down clue the pass is read upwards

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass
um is a hesitant noise meaning I'm not sure

explanation.surface: A footballer wonders if a high pass came from a substitute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lofted pass' sounds like football, but COL is a mountain pass, read upward.
explanation.definitionFit: A locum is a doctor or cleric standing in for another, a temporary replacement.

clue.text: Pop's nursing home rejected male model

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the letters are read in reverse
nursing means holding, so the drink holds the word for home

parts.note: pop is soda, a fizzy drink; the 's is 'has'
in means at home

explanation.surface: Dad's care home turned away a male fashion model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pop' looks like dad, but it is fizzy SODA.
explanation.definitionFit: Adonis, the beautiful youth of Greek myth, stands for any very handsome man, a pattern of male beauty.

clue.text: Ferret's food

definitions.meaning: to ferret is to rummage or dig about; the 's is 'is'

explanation.definitionFit: To grub is to dig and rummage like a ferret, and grub is also slang for food.

clue.text: Singer, or first to interrupt singer

indicators.note: to interrupt means the middle pieces break into the singer's name

parts.note: Cher is the American pop singer
1st, written IST, is first

explanation.surface: A singer, or rather the first to cut in on another singer.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'singer' is the American pop star Cher; 'first' is written as 1ST with the digit read as I.
explanation.definitionFit: A chorister is a member of a choir, so a vocalist.

clue.text: Don't take that which may be taken

definitions.meaning: to ... something is not to take it
holiday time off work, which one takes

explanation.definitionFit: To leave behind is not to take, and annual holiday entitlement from work is taken by staff.

clue.text: That is Bill, wet after squash club

indicators.note: after means the first group of words follows the word for squash

parts.note: to mash is to squash
ie, id est, means that is
a nib is a bird's bill or beak
to lick is to wet with the tongue

explanation.surface: A man called Bill gets soaked after playing squash at his club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Squash' looks like the racket game but is MASH; 'club' is a golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: A mashie-niblick is an old golf iron, equivalent to a seven iron.
